items.title: Export/extract readGitStatusLines + add the clean-tree preflight to review_run_start
items.context: (1) In done-oracle.ts, readGitStatusLines is private (line ~75) -- export it OR extract the git status --porcelain read + the classify/evaluate path into a small shared helper, WITHOUT changing the DONE gate verdict logic. (2) In the review_run_start handler (handlers/review-run.ts / core/review-run.ts), after the REVIEW phase check and BEFORE capturing the review-run snapshot, evaluate the working tree via that shared path (classifyGitStatusRows with dirtyWorktreeClassifierOptionsForStory + evaluateDirtyGate over DIRTY_GATE_POLICY). Refuse when the evaluation reports ANY BLOCKING category (material_source or fixture changes) with a clear actionable message (commit/revert code/config, then rerun review_run_start); the non-blocking categories (lattice_metadata / runtime_artifact / declared_artifact) pass. Do NOT change the DONE gate verdict, materialHash/currentMaterialHash computation, or the evidence-write-time freshness guard.

happy.desc: review_run_start on a clean worktree (no dirty files) -> succeeds and returns a ReviewRun ID; WHY: proves the preflight does not block when there is nothing dirty

review_run_start on a worktree with ONLY non-blocking dirty files (e.g. .lattice/stories/B-xxxx/index.json modified) -> succeeds; WHY: proves lattice_metadata_changes category passes through the preflight

done-oracle DONE-gate verdict is byte-identical after readGitStatusLines extraction -> buildDoneChecklist produces the same rows/status/blocking for a given story state; WHY: proves extraction did not alter DONE gate semantics

edge.desc: review_run_start when git status --porcelain is unreadable (e.g. not a git repo) -> fail-open, allows the review run to proceed; WHY: fail-open prevents the preflight from becoming a DOS vector when git is broken or the cwd is wrong
review_run_start with only runtime_artifact_changes dirty (e.g. .koala-serve.json) -> succeeds; WHY: proves runtime artifacts are non-blocking, matching DIRTY_GATE_POLICY
review_run_start with only declared_artifact_changes dirty -> succeeds; WHY: proves declared artifacts are non-blocking per DIRTY_GATE_POLICY

review_run_start with mixed non-blocking categories (lattice_metadata + runtime_artifact + declared_artifact all dirty) -> succeeds; WHY: multiple non-blocking categories simultaneously should not trip the gate

adversarial.desc: review_run_start with a single uncommitted material_source change (e.g. packages/main/src/core/foo.ts) -> REFUSES with actionable message naming the file; WHY: the core blocking scenario -- a reviewer must not snapshot drifting source
review_run_start with a single uncommitted fixture change -> REFUSES with actionable message; WHY: fixture drift is blocking in DIRTY_GATE_POLICY, must be caught

review_run_start with BOTH blocking AND non-blocking dirty files (material_source + lattice_metadata) -> REFUSES and names only the blocking files; WHY: mixed dirty state must still block, and the message must be actionable (not listing metadata as the problem)

review_run_start with unexpected_dirty_files (an untracked non-source file not matching any category) -> REFUSES; WHY: unexpected_dirty_files is BLOCKING in DIRTY_GATE_POLICY; the preflight must not silently allow unknown dirt through
review_run_start called when story is NOT in REVIEW phase -> rejects with phase error BEFORE the dirty-tree check runs; WHY: the phase guard must remain first; preflight must not mask the phase error

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke (c): clean tree -> review_run_start PROCEEDS and records RR-001.
Smoke (d): only .lattice metadata dirty -> PROCEEDS (non-blocking lattice_metadata category), with a pre-condition assert that isBlockingDirty(classification).blocked===false.
Smoke (g) regression: buildDoneChecklist git-working-tree row is unchanged after the readGitStatusLines extraction (DONE verdict byte-identical).
Smoke (h): unreadable git status (non-git dir -> readGitStatusLines ok:false) -> preflight fails open, does NOT block.

Covered by construction + parity: isBlockingDirty derives 'blocked' from DIRTY_GATE_POLICY[cat].blocking; runtime_artifact_changes is blocking:false (same as the directly-tested lattice_metadata). Smoke (d)+(f) exercise the non-blocking pass-through path and parity vs the DONE gate. Directly dirtying a runtime-artifact path needs registry fixtures and adds no soundness beyond the shared policy table.

Covered by construction + parity: declared_artifact_changes is blocking:false in DIRTY_GATE_POLICY (same path as the tested lattice_metadata); isBlockingDirty reads that table and the parity test (f) proves it matches the DONE gate. Directly dirtying a declared-artifact requires an artifact_declare fixture and adds no soundness beyond the policy table.
Smoke (d) + parity (f): multiple non-blocking categories pass because isBlockingDirty only flips on a blocking category; the parity table's non-blocking row confirms blocked===false.
Smoke (a): a single uncommitted material_source change (packages/main/src/foo.ts) -> review_run_start REFUSES (exit!=0), names material_source_changes + the file, no run recorded.
Smoke (b): a single uncommitted fixture change (tests/fixtures/sample.json) -> REFUSES, names fixture_changes + the file, no run recorded.
Smoke parity (f) mixed row: a status mixing a blocking material-source change + a non-blocking metadata change -> isBlockingDirty.blocked===true (blocking wins), matching the DONE gate.
Smoke parity (f) 'unexpected' row: an untracked non-source file (?? random/path/thing.bin) classifies as unexpected_dirty_files -> blocked===true, matching the DONE gate.

Structural: the preflight is placed in review_run_start AFTER the pre-existing REVIEW phase check (handlers/review-run.ts ~line 61, unchanged) and BEFORE captureReviewRunSnapshot; a non-REVIEW story is rejected by the phase check before the preflight runs. The phase guard is pre-existing behavior, untouched by this story.

items.title: Smoke + verifier wiring for the review_run_start clean-tree preflight
items.context: Add a smoke (packages/main/src/tasks/*-smoke.ts, auto-discovered by run-all-smokes) + npm script asserting: (a) review_run_start REFUSES on an uncommitted material-source change; (b) REFUSES on an uncommitted fixture change (fixtures are BLOCKING, matching the DONE gate); (c) PASSES when the tree is clean; (d) PASSES when only .lattice metadata (a non-blocking category) is dirty; (e) the refusal names the offending files; (f) the preflight yields the SAME blocking verdict as the DONE gate for an identical git status (shared evaluation).

happy.desc: smoke: review_run_start REFUSES on an uncommitted material_source change -> exits with blocking error naming the dirty source file; WHY: primary refuse path for the most common blocking category

smoke: review_run_start REFUSES on an uncommitted fixture change -> exits with blocking error naming the dirty fixture file; WHY: fixtures are BLOCKING in DIRTY_GATE_POLICY, smoke must assert parity with DONE gate

smoke: review_run_start PASSES when the worktree is clean (git status --porcelain returns empty) -> returns a valid ReviewRun ID; WHY: clean-tree happy path must not be broken by the preflight addition

smoke: review_run_start PASSES when only .lattice metadata is dirty -> returns a valid ReviewRun ID; WHY: metadata-only dirtiness (lattice_metadata_changes) is non-blocking per DIRTY_GATE_POLICY, must not trigger preflight refusal

smoke: refusal message names the offending file paths -> the error thrown by the preflight includes the actual dirty file path(s) so the operator knows what to commit/revert; WHY: actionable error messages are a key UX property

edge.desc: smoke: preflight yields the SAME blocking verdict as the DONE gate for an identical git-status input -> evaluateDirtyGate called with same classification + DIRTY_GATE_POLICY produces identical allPass/blockingCounts; WHY: shared evaluation is the architectural invariant -- divergence means the preflight disagrees with DONE about what blocks

smoke: DONE-gate regression -- buildDoneChecklist still produces the same git-working-tree row verdict as before the extraction; WHY: the extraction must be transparent; if DONE gate breaks, the whole workflow is broken

smoke: fail-open when git status is unreadable (readGitStatusLines returns ok:false) -> review_run_start proceeds instead of crashing; WHY: unreadable git status should not block the entire review workflow, matching fail-open design
smoke: npm script wiring -- the smoke file is auto-discovered by run-all-smokes and exits 0 on a passing run; WHY: CI integration requirement per checklist context

adversarial.desc: smoke: review_run_start with ALL three blocking categories dirty simultaneously (material_source + fixture + unexpected) -> REFUSES and the message includes counts/paths for each blocking category; WHY: multi-category blocking must aggregate, not short-circuit after the first category

smoke: blocking file with a git-quoted path containing unicode (e.g. renamed file with special chars) -> preflight still identifies it as blocking and names it in the error; WHY: git porcelain v1 quotes non-ASCII paths; the classifier must handle unquoting

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke (a): review_run_start REFUSES on an uncommitted material_source change (exit!=0).
Smoke (b): review_run_start REFUSES on an uncommitted fixture change (exit!=0, names fixture_changes).
Smoke (c): clean tree -> review_run_start PASSES and records exactly one run.
Smoke (d): only .lattice metadata dirty -> review_run_start PASSES (returns a started run).
Smoke (a)/(e): the refusal message names the offending file path (asserted via regex on packages/main/src/foo.ts).
Smoke (f) PARITY: isBlockingDirty(classifyGitStatusRows(...)) yields the SAME blocked verdict as the DONE gate's evaluateDirtyGitStatus for identical statuses.
Smoke (g) REGRESSION: buildDoneChecklist still produces the same git-working-tree classification/blocking after the extraction.
Smoke (h): fail-open when readGitStatusLines returns ok:false (unreadable git status).
npm script test:review-run-clean-tree-preflight runs the smoke (exit 0); run-all-smokes auto-discovers dist/tasks/*-smoke.js and the full npm test passed exit 0.

Smoke parity (f): all blocking categories present (material_source + fixture + unexpected rows each expectBlocked:true) -> isBlockingDirty aggregates (does not short-circuit) and blocks; matches the DONE gate.

Git-quoted / unicode path parsing is the responsibility of the shared classifyGitStatusRows (dirty-worktree.ts), which this preflight REUSES rather than re-implementing; quoted-path handling is covered by that upstream classifier's own tests, not re-asserted in this preflight smoke.
